_doc: What the narrative scripts need to know about this project. Every script takes --project <root> and reads <root>/narrative/.

fonts: name -> ttf, relative to the project root. boxes: every place a line can show, with the font, the size, the inner width in px and the lines that fit; lines null means the box is sized to the text's own newlines and any wrap is an overflow. prefix is text the engine puts before the line (the bark box prints the speaker).

budget: caps per box; the barks' cap is the count of story beats, not a number typed. engine: the table export.py writes, the source dirs lint.py --source greps for every id, the class the ids hang off, the file's doc comment. scenes: the order the sections are written in.

Derived on 2026-09-14 from game/src/ui/dialogue_box.gd (panel anchors 0.15..0.85 of 1920 = 1344 px, margins 24 = 1296 inner; height 0.72..0.94 of 1080 = 237.6, minus margins 48, the speaker at 24 px (25 high), the hint at 18 px (19 high) and two separations of 10 = 125.6 px for the body; VT323 at 28 px is 29 px a line, so 4 lines), bark_box.gd (anchors 0.1..0.9 = 1536 px, 0.86..0.92 = 64.8 px, VT323 at 26 px is 27 a line, so 2 lines, and the box prints `DANI — ` first) and sign.gd as make_stacks.gd sets it for a notice (width 240 minus 16 = 224 px at 12 px, the plate sized to the text's newlines).

bark._prefix: bark_box.gd prints the short name upper-cased and a dash before the line; VT323 is monospaced, so the case does not change the width

budget._doc: hook.md: a handful of protagonist lines in the whole slice; scarcity is what makes them land. The cap is the count of story beats that earn one: wake, first save, six pickups and the install, the chip, the quest, before and after the boss.

header: Every written line in the slice (docs/narrative/hook.md).
The protagonist talks Castlevania-style: a handful of terse lines at story
beats, never a tree, never a choice. Scarcity is what makes them land, so
this file is deliberately short. Tone: working-class cyberpunk — paycheck
dread, gallows humour, the debt statement as the scariest artifact.
